steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: This herd is incredibly tough.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Not only do these mutated Sarkaz Infected have much better healing capabilities than normal possessed Infected, they are much more intelligent, too.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: But that still doesn't give us a way to actually talk to them. They all seem so... strange. Like they're all in some place else.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: Not only that, this type of mutation is an accident waiting to happen. The crystals form way too fast.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The concentration of crystal dust in the air is the highest right here.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That probably means that whoever is controlling the Herd here has most likely taken over the sarcophagus of the Chernobog core city already.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Things are always happening in places we don't have our eyes on.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: I really can't even begin to imagine what we'll be facing from here on out.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: ...I don't mind getting an earful for this, Doctor, but I have to say this. This is way too difficult.

steps.name: Rhodes Island Operator
steps.text: What we are doing might just be suicide. And, most importantly, I really don't think we have what it takes to save this city and Lungmen.

options: There are still things we need to do.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Chard, if memory serves, you have a family, don't you?

steps.name: Chard
steps.text: I'm surprised you remember, Doctor. You got one detail wrong, though. My wife and my daughter don't care about me anymore, so I don't really have one.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Chard, have you ever thought about seeing them, and start living with them once again?

steps.name: Chard
steps.text: I dreamed about it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The first step to turning your dreams into reality is to give yourself the chance to dream.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Stopping Chernobog isn't going to make life any harder for the Infected.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Give your daughter a chance, Chard. Give her the chance to see her father again.

steps.name: Chard
steps.text: I'll do as you say, Doctor.

options: You're just taking him for a ride.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What I said may have been a lie. I don't think the world is going to become a better place overnight, and there's basically no way the Infected will get to go back to their previous lives.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But what I said could also be the truth.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Suppose we leave this place right now. He will never have the chance to see his daughter again, regardless of whether his family or he himself die of other causes in the events that will transpire.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And suppose we aren't able to solve the problem we are facing right now. Most broader academic research will forever remain theories and nothing more.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The successes of those who put in the work is what gives us the right to continue.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There are countless people trying to revolutionize the system for the Infected, but all it takes is one failure, and not only will they forever lose the right to try that, we will never again have that opportunity again.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you need a more suitable metaphor, consider the concept, 'life'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Each time a major operation ends in success, we live to see another day. On the other hand, failure means death.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There is no such thing as coming back from the dead in science.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We only have one chance to save our lives. We will come to face many disasters, and it will be the end of us each time an accident happens. That's both ourselves individually or Rhodes Island as a whole.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Disasters like Chernobog are bound to happen again and again. If we fail to solve a problem like that even once, we will die.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: On one hand, we have to stop the disease before it catches up and overwhelms all of us. On the other hand, we need to save ourselves from within this storm.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm not singing Rhodes Island's praises. Not too much, at least. It's just, right here, right now, this is a problem that only we can handle.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Most of us only get to live once. Once our lives are lost, it's gone forever.

options: You mean there are people who gets to live several lives?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Uh, that's not really what I'm trying to say. What I mean is that there are people who haven't ever treasured their own lives.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There are a lot of people who have never been around anything normal ever since they were born. Twisted places will only bear twisted fruits.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The reason there is so much malice in Chernobog is precisely because there has always been malice not kept in check there.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Malice, or more precisely, all those chains of malice aren't going to disappear on their own.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Each destruction, each killing might only have been caused by a modicum of desire. In a lawless land, barbarism is simply left to breed rampantly on its own, and that is how it becomes the law of the land.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And this kind of law is much stronger than the law you'd find in the cities. It's simply indestructible.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's violence. The violence that flows in our blood veins comes from the parts of us left untamed by civilization.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Listen.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Did you hear that...?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Singing...?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: How peculiar. Originium Arts don't usually interfere with my senses at all.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: All operators, put on your protective equipment!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, something terrible might be happening.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Based on the chaos we've seen along the way, we probably would've reached this conclusion all the same, but I'm afraid what we are about to face might be far worse than what we could ever have imagined.

options: Has it ever gone any other way?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I wouldn't say it's always a foregone conclusion.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps someone has placed a curse on either us or this city. That being said, curses can be broken.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you plant the seeds of evil, the flowers of evil will blossom, bearing fruits of evil. If we water the earth with goodwill, then even if this parcel of land doesn't get any better... at least it wouldn't meet such a dreadful fate and be buried by a tragedy like this.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's a shame...
You look in the same direction as Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's a shame that, as far as I know, evil is a vicious cycle that will only breed even worse malice, and fate is rarely kind to those who are kind at heart.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I can't allow you to bring about yet another nightmare, Infected.
